prompts.name: invalidate_edge

prompts.name: resolve_entity@batch

prompts.name: summarize (+@brief, @detailed, @incremental, @structured)

prompts.name: relevance
prompts.summary: LLM rerank-style labelling relevant / related / irrelevant per note; notes as JSON lines inside nonce markers.

prompts.name: sufficiency / @missing / @agentic / @agentic_slot

prompts.name: chat (+@dated, @dated2, @dated3, @infer, @inference, @temporal)

prompts.name: grounded_generic (+ _infer, _list, _prefs; routed_generic)
prompts.summary: Harness reader without dataset wording: memories optional, newest wins unless asked about the past, relative times against line date, exact refusal string; routed by question shape.

F1.t: window_extract keeps the expression and appends the absolute date: 'last Friday (YYYY-MM-DD)'; session prompts rewrite to ISO and fill `date`.

F2.t: Every transcript line carries [n] [YYYY-MM-DD]; dates are computed from the line's own date, not the run date.

F3.t: Facts carry a speaker field; episode narrative attributes every statement to its speaker; edges map 'I' to the speaker.

F4.t: Separate subject and persons fields beside speaker (facts section).

F5.t: Rule 7: a plan, wish, hedge or question is not a fact and must be marked ('plans to'); no negation or opinion field, modality only in prose.

F6.t: Every item cites `turns`; facts also give a verbatim `span`; an item without a supporting line is disallowed.

F7.t: Fact extractors see no existing memories; only extract_edges gets known entity names and earlier episodes (names, no ids); resolve_entity@batch uses numbered candidates.

F8.t: state vs event kind tells the store a newer value replaces; invalidate_edge gives add/update/invalidate/noop; no 'changed from X to Y' transition fact at extraction.

F9.t: No 'skip what is already known' rule (extractor never sees the store); duplicates are left to a separate dedupe prompt and code; edges merge multi-line mentions.

F10.t: Episode title <=12 words, summary <=50, narrative 40-300; entity summary <=1,000 chars; no bound on a fact's value.

F11.t: Coverage push for facts ('Cover every fact, not a summary', every list item, every countable occurrence); precision push for edges ('when in doubt ... do not extract').

F12.t: Never he/she/they or 'the user'; resolve every pronoun and 'that'/'it'.

F13.t: Episode narrative is a chronological third-person account; facts name people.

F14.t: kind state/event plus an open attribute vocabulary (city, job, hobby, plan, preference, relationship) and a topic class; no closed type taxonomy.

F15.t: confidence 0-1 on facts and edges; no importance score.

F16.t: Pydantic output_model per prompt, JSON or YAML only; per-section validation; code-side json-repair net, no in-prompt repair re-ask.

F17.t: Shared no_injection partial in every prompt; relevance wraps notes in nonce markers.

F18.t: One invented single-line example per prompt (made-up names); a CI gold-lint denies known benchmark strings and speaker names.

F19.t: No same-language or multilingual rule in any default prompt.

F20.t: token_budget per prompt sent as max_tokens (160-4096); window writer at temperature 0; harness readers default 0.0.

F21.t: Exact refusal string, inference clause for would/likely, said-vs-happened dates, granularity rule, merge-before-count, short answer; date arithmetic delegated to code in the agentic step.

F22.t: Static system block, variable transcript/question last in the user part; window system text varies only with the configured sections.

F23.t: window_extract produces facts, edges and episode in one call, each validated separately; split mode re-renders with fewer sections.

F1.t: Extraction converts all relative times to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) inside the restatement and a timestamp field; Graphiti edges resolve valid_at/invalid_at from REFERENCE_TIME; planner resolves query time phrases to ISO ranges.

F2.t: Each dialogue line is rendered '[timestamp] speaker: content'; Graphiti episodes use each message's own timestamp as reference_time.

F3.t: Graphiti always extracts the speaker as first entity; dev_mem tells it the message format is role-prefixed; SimpleMem entries list persons.

F4.t: 'you/your' rewritten to 'the user', persons list separate from speaker prefix; no explicit about-whom field.

F5.t: No modality/negation rule; the dev_mem custom instruction actually turns any asking/interest into a factual edge, conflating intent with fact.

F6.t: No citations required; dialogue ids are computed but not requested in model output; answers cite nothing.

F7.t: Graphiti dedupe shows existing facts and invalidation candidates with continuous integer idx, existing entities as JSON; SimpleMem shows only the first 3 previous-window restatements, without ids.

F8.t: Graphiti marks contradicted_facts (a fact may be duplicate AND superseded) and sets invalid_at on expressed changes; profile rebuild re-derives sections.

F9.t: SimpleMem: previous entries shown 'to avoid duplication'; Graphiti: 'Do not emit duplicate or semantically redundant facts' plus dedupe prompts; profile 'Merge overlapping topics'.

F10.t: Hard word caps on session summary (max_words) and user profile; Graphiti entity summary character cap; no per-fact length bound.

F11.t: Coverage push: 'Extract all valuable information', 'enough entries to capture ALL', and edges MUST be extracted for any user interest; light precision clause drops greetings/trivia.

F12.t: 'Never use pronouns (he, she, it, they, this, that)'; Graphiti disambiguates pronouns to entity names.

F13.t: 'ALL memories must be written in third-person perspective'; planner also rewrites queries to third person.

F14.t: Optional Graphiti entity types; fixed profile sections; free-text topic field. No fact/preference/event item taxonomy.

F15.t: Memories carry no confidence or importance; only the read-side completeness evaluator returns a coverage percentage.

F16.t: Inline JSON schemas and json_object mode; Graphiti uses pydantic response models; extraction retries on parse failure (raising in migration mode so failure is not read as 'nothing to extract'). No repair re-prompt text.

F17.t: Only the eval harness answer/judge prompts say supplied text is data; production extraction, summary and answer prompts have no anti-injection rule.

F18.t: Generic invented few-shot (meeting at a coffee shop) for extraction and answer; no benchmark content. The extraction example is internally inconsistent: its output dates the suggestion a day before the input timestamp. Reformulator examples are domain-flavoured.

F19.t: Vendored Graphiti client appends a same-language extraction instruction to the system message; dev_mem SimpleMem/summary prompts have no language rule.

F20.t: Extraction temperature 0.1, planner 0.2, reflection 0.1/0.3; summaries max_tokens 2000, profile 1200/1500; eval answer and judge temperature 0. Reformulator limits come from config (values not reproduced).

F21.t: Production: relevance check, fixed abstention string, context-only, fixed date format, no length limit ('every relevant information'). Eval harness: exact abstention string, historical not today's dates, all list items, concise; empty memories short-circuit to abstention without a call.

F22.t: Eval harness: static system prompt, variable JSON user message last. Production extraction puts previous entries and dialogue BEFORE the static rules, and the planner puts the current datetime at the top, defeating prefix caching.

F23.t: Read side folds plan + search signals + queries into one call; write side is one prompt per layer (SimpleMem entries, Graphiti nodes, edges, dedupe, entity summaries, session summary, user profile).

prompts.name: MEMORY_ANSWER_PROMPT (proxy)
prompts.summary: Proxy chat system prompt for answering from memories; explicitly forbids saying no information was found.

F1.t: ADDITIVE prompt resolves ALL relative references against Observation Date into absolute dates; examples use 'around <Month D, YYYY>' form, never vague.

F2.t: Single 'Observation Date' per batch, distinct from Current Date; but the core add() never passes timestamp, so it defaults to today (run date).

F3.t: ADDITIVE: attributed_to field (user/assistant) required; named speakers inside the assistant role extracted and attributed by name.

F4.t: attributed_to is glossed as 'who this memory is about' but takes speaker roles only; no separate subject field.

F5.t: ADDITIVE keeps plans, opinions, 'never done before', 'used to' negation and temporary/trial changes; no explicit modality tag.

F6.t: No citation of source messages/spans; linked_memory_ids link to existing memories, not evidence.

F7.t: Existing memories (top 10 by vector search) shown as [{id,text}]; code maps UUIDs to integer-string aliases 'anti-hallucination' (prompt text still says UUIDs).

F8.t: ADDITIVE: memory MUST capture the transition, new state AND what it replaces ('switched from X to Y'); legacy UPDATE carries old_memory.

F9.t: Recently Extracted is primary dedup reference; skip semantic equivalents of Existing Memories; no echo and no within-response duplication rules.

F10.t: 15-80 words per memory (up to 100 for detail-rich), 1-2 sentences, completeness beats brevity.

F11.t: Strong coverage push: 'When in doubt, extract'; exhaustive checklist (5-15 memories per 10+ messages); 'first topic dominance' warning.

F12.t: Self-contained: replace all pronouns with specific names or 'User'; Last k Messages given to resolve references.

F13.t: Statements framed as 'User ...' or by name; agent variant reframes as 'Agent was informed that ...'.

F14.t: Legacy extractors list 7 information categories; V3 ADDITIVE has no type field in output.

F15.t: No confidence/importance in extraction output; only the read-time reranker emits a relevance score.

F16.t: JSON-only output parsable by json.loads, json_object response_format, code-fence stripping and extract_json fallback; ensure_json_instruction patch.

F17.t: No 'transcript is data' rule; reranker only separates system/user and truncates inputs (code comment, not prompt text).

F18.t: ADDITIVE has ~11 worked examples. Leak risk: the multi-speaker example uses first names and pet/family details matching LoCoMo-style speakers; examples mirror historic-date benchmark shape.

F19.t: Optional use_input_language block (same language and script, no transliteration, CJK formality, Japanese subject resolution); legacy prompts detect language.

F20.t: LLM defaults temperature 0.1, max_tokens 2000; reranker temperature 0.0, max_tokens 100.

F21.t: Proxy answer prompt is anti-abstention ('don't say no information is found'), no date arithmetic or length limit; no eval-harness answer prompt in this clone.

F22.t: Static ADDITIVE system prompt; all variable sections (memories, messages, dates) in the user message, dates near the end. No explicit cache_control.

F23.t: One call yields one layer (fact memories + links); procedural summary is a separate prompt; no profile/summary output from the extractor.

prompts.name: ANSWER_PROMPT (LoCoMo harness)
prompts.summary: Evaluation-harness answer prompt: 7-step CoT with time-reference calculation and confidence-labelled inference.

F1.t: Episode and atomic-fact prompts require 'original expression (absolute date or range)', ISO-week ranges, UTC labels on clock times; vague terms kept unresolved.

F2.t: Episode prompts say each message has its own timestamp and resolve relative times against that message, not the session start; boundary log is per-message timestamped.

F3.t: Atomic-fact prompt demands explicit attribution of who said or did what (GOOD/BAD example).

F4.t: Profile prompts scope to one target speaker id and assign facts 'about another participant' to that participant; user-episode variant separates asker/recipient role.

F5.t: Agent-profile prompt classifies speech act (directive/question/venting/withdrawn/deferral/denial/material); profile excludes passing states; atomic facts keep plans/opinions.

F6.t: Quotes required, not ids: profile 'evidence' is up to two dated verbatim quotes; sufficiency check cites 'Source: Doc N'; topic tree carries paragraph block_refs.

F7.t: Profile update shows the stored profile with per-item integer indices (snapshot-stable index semantics); skill extraction shows indexed existing skills. Atomic-fact extractor is not neighbour-aware.

F8.t: Profile ops update (correction/contradiction) and delete (negated/expired/contradicted); reflect prompt 'resolves contradictions by keeping the latest state' and corrects outdated statements.

F9.t: Profile update: 'Adding a second copy of a fact already on file is always wrong'; scan stored items for the same fact under any wording before add.

F10.t: Episode title <20 words, summary 1-3 sentences (~50 words); foresight items <=40 words; profile items one or two short sentences; skill description <=150 tokens.

F11.t: Both, by layer: atomic facts push coverage ('Every meaningful fact is captured'); profile and agent-profile push precision ('When in doubt, emit nothing'; 'none' often correct); decider favours recall.

F12.t: Atomic facts resolve pronouns to names; episode prompt uses specific names rather than pronouns for retrieval.

F13.t: Atomic facts and episodes are written as third-person single sentences/narrative.

F14.t: Separate typed layers (episode, atomic fact, foresight, profile explicit_info vs implicit_traits, skill, case) rather than a per-fact type label; profile categories are free-form group keys.

F15.t: Confidence only in agent-side prompts: skill confidence anchoring (0.5 new, +0.1 per new branch, cap 0.95) and step-boundary confidence; no importance on user facts.

F16.t: Every prompt specifies exact JSON; profile update notes brace-count repair hint; SUMMARY_COMPRESS is a width-guard repair prompt; reflect uses Structured Output with summary field ordered after content.

F17.t: Only the agent-profile prompt treats instruction-shaped lines in pasted material as data ('a prompt-injection vector'); user-memory extractors have no such rule.

F18.t: Few-shot throughout (boundary, atomic facts, episode, foresight, decider). Leak risk: the atomic-fact and episode examples use LoCoMo speaker first names and LoCoMo-style events; the decider examples are declared invented.

F19.t: Measured language-rule module: caller-named language or participant-language rule spliced at head and tail; inheriting rules for update/compact/merge; names and ids kept verbatim.

F20.t: Default temperature 0.0 in LLM config; max_tokens unset by default (per-call override); prompt length validator exists but no per-prompt output cap.

F21.t: Only in the LoCoMo harness answer prompt: explicit time-reference calculation step and gap analysis, but it pushes inference ('Do not dismiss reasonable inferences') with confidence labels and no abstention rule or length limit.

F22.t: Profile prompts deliberately put instructions first and DATA LAST; episode and atomic-fact prompts interleave the conversation mid-prompt and wrap a language rule at both ends.

F23.t: Mostly one prompt per layer (episode, atomic fact, foresight, profile separate); topic-tree call produces the tree plus document summary/keywords together; episode emits title+content+summary in one call.

prompts.name: ANSWER_PROMPT_MEMOS (LoCoMo harness)
prompts.summary: Evaluation-harness answer prompt: latest memory wins, mandatory relative-date calculation, under 5-6 words.

F1.t: Reader converts relative times to absolute dates using the message timestamp (replacement, not dual format, e.g. 'On <date>'); uncertainty stated as 'around <month>', 'exact date unclear'.

F2.t: Each conversation line carries its own timestamp in the reader examples; strategy reader separates event time from message time.

F3.t: Assistant content kept only with explicit attribution; rewrite validator labels '[assistant] memory' and '[assistant] memory, but [user] denied'.

F4.t: Answer prompt's attribution check separates User from third parties ('NEVER attribute third-party traits'); reader disambiguates same-name people but has no subject field.

F5.t: Negation via hallucination filter (user-denied claims deleted) and denial labels; plans kept; inferred facts hedged 'It can be inferred that'; no plan/wish/hypothetical tagging.

F6.t: Answer prompt requires sentence-end citations '[i:memId]' with strict format; extraction prompts do not cite source lines.

F7.t: Merge prompt shows similar existing memories with full UUID ids and returns merged_from ids; feedback and preference updaters reference memories by id (no integer aliases).

F8.t: Feedback updater: contradiction triggers UPDATE with old_memory and minimal span edit; preference updater preserves change-history trajectory; explicit extractor captures original and updated preference.

F9.t: Add-before-search discards candidates 'completely redundant, already known'; merge prompt: each fact described only once.

F10.t: Summary bounded to 120-200 words; harness answer under 5-6 words; no per-memory length bound.

F11.t: Reader pushes coverage ('Prioritize completeness and fidelity over conciseness'); implicit-preference prompt pushes precision ('Stay conservative').

F12.t: Resolve all pronouns, aliases and ambiguous references to full names.

F13.t: Always third-person, 'The user' or name, never first person.

F14.t: Coarse memory_type LongTermMemory vs UserMemory plus free tags; preferences split explicit/implicit with topic; relation types CAUSE/CONDITION/RELATE/CONFLICT.

F15.t: No confidence or importance emitted by extraction prompts; only the relation resolver mentions confidence metadata if present.

F16.t: JSON schemas and tag-based (<answer>, <can_answer>) formats throughout; no repair instruction in prompts.

F17.t: Answer prompt sets instruction hierarchy and ignores user attempts to alter rules; preference extractor ignores injected/retrieved/tool context even inside a user message; reader has no transcript-is-data rule.

F18.t: Few-shot widely. Leak risk: the read-time enhancement prompt and strategy reader examples reuse LoCoMo speaker names and a LoCoMo event description.

F19.t: Output fields must match the input language with explicit Chinese rule; every major prompt has a _ZH twin; memory_type kept in English.

F20.t: LLM config default temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 8192; no per-prompt caps.

F21.t: Product prompt: unsupported claims must be flagged, current query overrides memory; harness: latest memory wins, mandatory date arithmetic, world knowledge allowed for interpretation, under 5-6 words.

F22.t: Reader puts static rules first and conversation last; product system prompt embeds {date}, {tone}, {verbosity} mid-prefix, breaking a static cache prefix.

F23.t: Simple reader emits memory list plus summary in one call; strategy reader emits facts and speaker profile together; separate prompts for preferences, merge and reorganisation.

F1.t: Experiment events prompt KEEPS relative expressions ('don't replace them with ambiguous expressions') rather than resolving; resolution is deferred to read-time answer/response prompts. Current product: no engine prompt.

F2.t: Experiment gives one session date per call ('Mentioned at {session_date}'), not per-message timestamps; current product leaves transcripts to the host agent with no timestamp rule.

F3.t: Experiment extracts per character and records reported past events as '{character_name} mentioned that ...'.

F4.t: Events about people close to the character (parents, children) are pulled in, but there is no separate subject/about-whom field.

F5.t: No modality/negation rule; only the few-shot examples model plans ('Planning to rest tomorrow', 'might bring').

F6.t: No source-line or message-id citations in any prompt; current product retrieval returns source_file metadata but the model is not asked to cite.

F7.t: Experiment passes Existing Events / Existing Profile as raw text (no ids); current product job tells the agent to read existing file NAMES first and bodies only if related (referenced by filename).

F8.t: Profile prompt: update when newer/more specific; current job: patch existing file in place. No explicit 'changed from X to Y' transition form.

F9.t: Experiment: 'Focus only on NEW information not already present'; current product prefers no-op or patching over near-duplicate files.

F10.t: No per-memory length bound; only the answer is capped (<=20 words) and profile asks 'concise'; resource descriptions 'one to several sentences'.

F11.t: Experiment is a strong COVERAGE push (every message, 'no matter how minor') plus a verifier/refine loop; current product is a PRECISION push ('A no-op is a perfectly good outcome').

F12.t: No explicit no-pronoun / coreference rule in any prompt.

F13.t: 'Use third-person perspective consistently' in event extraction and refine prompts.

F14.t: Two stores (events vs profile) and a fixed 5-category profile schema; current product splits memory / skill / resource. No per-item type labels.

F15.t: Only the verifier/sufficiency deciders return a 0-1 confidence; memories carry no importance score.

F16.t: JSON only for deciders and query rewrite; extraction outputs free-text paragraphs / markdown; current product mandates YAML front-matter. No repair instructions.

F17.t: No 'transcript is data' / ignore-embedded-instructions rule in experiment prompts or current host-agent job templates.

F18.t: Few-shot outputs with generic invented names (restaurant lunch, marathon, sample profile); no benchmark dialogue copied. Note the experiment folder's memory/ directory stores benchmark run outputs (data, not prompts).

F20.t: Experiment: extraction max_tokens 4000 at temperature 0.3; sufficiency 1000 / 0.1; answer 8000 / 0.2. Current product sets none (host agent).

F21.t: Experiment answer prompt: think-then-result, date-arithmetic step relative to mention time, include ALL scattered answers, state what is missing if insufficient, <=20 words.

F22.t: Experiment prompts interleave variables early (question/character first); no static prefix. Current product's retrieval instruction is a static managed block in the host instruction file, but that is the host's prompt.

F23.t: One prompt per layer: events and profile are separate calls (then verifier, refine, clean). Current skill job bundles skill writing with resource logging only.

F1.t: Read-time notes and bench notes resolve 'yesterday/last week' to absolute dates from the excerpt/session date; consolidation stamps each item with a YYYY/MM/DD session date field (not inline 'expression (date)').

F2.t: Every record in a fold carries its own header with session date and session number; bench seeding prefixes each turn with its date and speaker. Session-date granularity, not wall-clock time.

F3.t: User vs assistant kept (assistant proposals only when the user relied on them); bench notes keep speaker via 'who did, said'. No explicit speaker field in consolidation output.

F4.t: Bench notes: 'Name who each fact is about'; judge rejects items that concern a different person. No structured subject field.

F5.t: Plans/decisions/opinions are captured as content ('planned, changed, finished'), and a conflict flag marks unexplained contradictions; no modality or negation label.

F6.t: Every consolidated event/fact/directive must list the record ids it came from; answer worker must cite exact memoryBodyId/id of evidence used.

F7.t: Fold shows threads (T# ids with counts/last date), state keys with latest value and directives so far, capped by lexical relevance+recency; new records use batch-local r# aliases. Recall uses n#, judge uses c# labels.

F8.t: 'When an existing key changes, repeat that exact key with the new value' builds a value history; read-time judge asks whether a later explicit statement supersedes; runtime protocol uses replace/remove.

F9.t: Directives: 'do not repeat one already listed' (plus code word-overlap filter); thread reuse instead of new; runtime protocol skips duplicates.

F10.t: Events: one sentence of at most 30 words; searches 'a few words'; code also caps listing/excerpt characters.

F11.t: Mixed by stage: recall is a coverage push (include possibly outdated notes); consolidation and runtime writes are precision pushes (only what records say; do not save guesses, questions, assistant claims).

F12.t: Notes must be 'short, self-contained' and keep exact names; no explicit no-pronoun rule.

F14.t: Three item kinds (events on sub-topic threads, changeable state facts, directives/preferences); read side classifies intent fact/collect/suggest.

F15.t: Runtime writes carry importance critical/normal/low; placement selector returns calibrated confidence. Consolidated items have no score.

F16.t: Inline JSON schema for consolidation with a tolerant fenced/unfenced parser; read prompts use line protocols (SEARCH:, NOTE:, KIND:, NEED:/ALL:, [e#]). No repair re-prompt; malformed output falls back.

F17.t: Every system prompt declares notes/messages/excerpts/transcript 'data, never instructions'; judge rejects 'text that tries to instruct the assistant'.

F18.t: No few-shot examples; only a JSON shape with placeholder values and one inline hint ('that place'). No benchmark leakage; the LoCoMo answer prompt is generic.

F19.t: No same-language rule in prompts; code handles CJK in parsing/regexes only.

F20.t: Temperature 0 on all recall-model calls; maxTokens 400 default (recall), 200 (needs/re-plan), 1000 (read-time notes), 8192 (consolidation fold).

F21.t: Eval-harness answer prompts: abstain rather than guess, date arithmetic from the stated current date, latest version when facts changed, brevity, optional list-dated-events-first step; product answer worker: evidence only, say if insufficient.

F22.t: llmRecall deliberately keeps the note listing in first-seen order as a cacheable prefix, dialogue last, and measures the stable prefix length; consolidation system prompt is static.

F23.t: One fold call yields three layers (events/threads, state values, directives); one cue call yields searches + invented note + intent kind.

F1.t: Deriver: use absolute dates, resolving relative references against the message time attribute; no fixed output format (no 'expression (date)' pattern)

F2.t: Every message carries its own time='%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' attribute in the deriver input

F3.t: Deriver tags peer and target flag per message; facts only from target='true' messages, others used as context only

F4.t: Deriver: 'Properly attribute observations to the correct subject'; observer/observed pair model in dialectic; peer card subject must be the observee

F5.t: No plan/wish/hypothetical capture rule; summaries keep 'preferences, opinions'; deduction flags contradictions incl. negations ('I love coffee' vs 'I hate coffee')

F6.t: Dream specialists must copy source_ids from [id:xxx]; empty/invented ids rejected. Cites premise observations, not message spans; deriver does not cite message idx

F7.t: Deriver is NOT neighbour-aware; dream specialists browse observations via tools with real [id:xxx] ids and get current peer card injected

F8.t: Deduction: same fact with different values -> create deductive update observation and DELETE outdated one; dialectic: more recent statement supersedes

F9.t: Deriver: no two conclusions stating same fact; deduction: delete outdated, no duplicates; peer card: full deduplicated list

F10.t: Per-item: one fact per conclusion, only what is needed to identify subject; peer card entries one concise fact, max 40 entries; summaries target_tokens

F11.t: Both: deriver 'Extract ALL observations' from target messages and summariser 'capture as many explicit facts as possible' (coverage); deduction 'Quality over quantity' (precision)

F12.t: Deriver: leave no pronoun, 'it', 'there', or relative time unresolved; identify others by relation to this peer

F13.t: Deriver: write peer id as subject of every observation, never 'the user' or 'the target peer'

F14.t: Levels explicit/deductive/inductive; inductive pattern_type preference|behavior|personality|tendency|correlation; peer card IDENTITY/ATTRIBUTE/RELATIONSHIP/INSTRUCTION

F15.t: Induction confidence low/medium/high computed from evidence count (2 / 3-4 / 5+ sources); no score at deriver

F16.t: Deriver: json_mode with pydantic PromptRepresentation and 3 retries; dream: tool-call schemas, rejection of empty/invented source_ids and unprefixed card entries

F17.t: Structural only: content-level '<message' tags escaped so a message cannot forge tag boundaries; no textual 'transcript is data' instruction

F18.t: Inline illustrative examples only (deduction implications, peer card prefixes, abstention CORRECT/WRONG); generic, no benchmark names

F19.t: No multilingual or same-language rule in deriver, dreamer, summariser or dialectic prompts

F20.t: Deriver max_tokens = model max_output_tokens or DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (2500); dream specialists 8192 (base 16384) and 10-15 tool iterations; temperature configurable, default None

F21.t: Dialectic: confident 'I don't know' always correct, never fabricate; present both sides of contradictions; enumeration verification/dedup; no explicit date-arithmetic step or length limit

F22.t: Deriver: static instructions first, peer id and messages last; dream: static system + variable user prompt. Dialectic interleaves peer cards before tool/workflow text (less cacheable)

F23.t: Separate prompts per layer (explicit deriver, summary, deduction, induction, card); deduction run can write observations, deletions and peer card in one agent loop

F1.t: CRM domain prompt only: relative dates to ISO/EDTF, '[EDTF_date] content' value prefix, event date preferred over message date; default profile prompt has no date rule.

F2.t: Summary and CoQ inputs carry per-episode '[date at time] producer:' lines; the semantic extractor gets raw message content only, and CRM uses a build-time CURRENT_DATE.

F3.t: Speaker (producer_id) appears in summary input lines; CRM has an author field; semantic update sees no speaker label.

F4.t: CRM separates tag (company the entry is about) from author (who reported it); generic profile assumes subject = user.

F5.t: Update prompt warns not to drop negations/qualifiers and to hedge uncertain inferences in the value; profile lists negative preference cues ('I avoid').

F6.t: Consolidation outputs metadata.citations (ids of old memories that influenced it); CoQ outputs evidence_indices over retrieved docs. No message-span citations at extraction.

F7.t: Update sees the full current profile keyed by tag/feature (no ids); consolidation sees similar memories with integer metadata.id and returns keep-ids.

F8.t: Update = delete then add of a feature; CRM single-valued fields use delete-then-add; no 'changed from X to Y' wording; 'do not delete unless asked'.

F9.t: Consolidation deletes redundant memories and merges similar ones; CRM status dedupe against the latest status.

F10.t: Entries atomic and 'as short as possible without corrupting meaning'; no numeric per-item bound (summary has a word cap).

F11.t: Coverage push: 'wide early layer' doing edge detection, make inferences, include uncertain entries, extract ALL personal information.

F12.t: No pronoun/coreference rule at write time; only the read-side split prompt adds a pronoun-resolution sub-query.

F13.t: Example values are written as 'User ...' but there is no explicit third-person rule.

F14.t: Fixed tag taxonomy (37 profile tags; 'do not create new tags', features free) plus domain categories.

F15.t: Write-time confidence only as hedged wording in the value; numeric confidence_score with anchors exists in read-time CoQ.

F16.t: JSON command lists parsed via pydantic output_format; CoQ extracts last brace block with retry. Mismatch: prompt shows a bare list and key 'consolidate_memories' while schemas expect 'commands' and 'consolidated_memories'.

F17.t: No anti-injection rule; CRM's 'only extract from USER INPUT, not existing profile' is about contamination, not injection.

F18.t: Few-shot in update, CRM, split and router prompts; no LoCoMo text in engine prompts, but CRM examples embed apparently real company/contact data (internal-data leak risk).

F19.t: No language rule in any engine prompt.

F20.t: Summary capped 'under {max_length} words'; split output 1-6 lines; no engine default temperature/max tokens (eval judge at 0.0).

F21.t: Eval-harness answer prompts: date arithmetic from timestamps, most-recent-wins, under 5-6 words; no abstention, one prompt invites guessing. CoQ: uncertain means insufficient.

F22.t: Update/consolidation use a static per-category system prompt with variables in the user message; CRM bakes the date at the top; router/CoQ interpolate variables mid-template in one user prompt.

F23.t: Read-side CoQ merges sufficiency, evidence citation, confidence and rewrite in one call; write side is one call per semantic category per message.

F1.t: Episodic occurred_at is a required absolute 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' tool field; no instruction to rewrite relative expressions in text

F2.t: Accumulator prefixes each message with 'Timestamp: {ts}'; system prompt also carries Current Time in user timezone

F10.t: Block-level budgets: core blocks 5000 chars (rewrite to ~2500), avoid appending to events over 5000 chars; summary <100 words; no per-fact bound

F11.t: Coverage push: meta prefers including extra memory types; core 'extract EVERY detail'; episodic 'record as many details as possible' (but one call per batch)

F14.t: Six memory types (core, episodic, procedural, resource, knowledge vault, semantic) with routing rules; plus event_type, entry_type, skill entry_type

F8.t: State changes update the observation to current state with dates, cascade to list observations, preserve history; worked supersede-and-delete example.

F9.t: Retain: 'Repeated info: if already stated, don't extract again'; consolidation prefers UPDATE over CREATE, at most one update per observation_id.

F10.t: 'what' is 1-2 sentences max; 'one good sentence beats three mediocre ones'.

F11.t: Default concise mode is a precision push ('Be SELECTIVE', useful in 6 months?); verbose mode is a coverage push; attachment rule demands every chart value.

F12.t: Coreference section links generic relations to names, e.g. 'Name (user's roommate)'.

F13.t: No explicit rewrite rule; examples render facts in third person ('User planning ...').

F14.t: fact_kind event/conversation and fact_type world/assistant, plus configurable entity label taxonomy.

F15.t: No confidence or importance requested; proof_count is computed, not judged.

F16.t: Pydantic json_schema (optionally strict) response_format; shape-repair re-ask lists keys used vs valid keys; auto-split on output overflow.

F17.t: No 'content is data' rule in retain or consolidation; reflect only has 'use tool results only' anti-hallucination grounding.

F18.t: Generic few-shots with an explicit guard 'never emit their facts... unless they appear in the input'; no LoCoMo speaker names seen.

F19.t: Same language and script as input, never translate; consolidation picks per-observation majority language; optional forced output language.

F20.t: Temperatures: retain 0.1, consolidation 0.0, reflect 0.9; retain max_completion_tokens 64000; soft visible-length directive for answers.

F21.t: Say the data does not record it rather than invent; infer qualitatively but never manufacture values; latest mentioned_at wins; KEEP/DROP date audit with explicit arithmetic; current date given.

F22.t: Explicitly designed: bank mission moved out of the system prompt into the user turn so one cached prefix serves all banks (retain and consolidation).

F11.t: Precision push for semantic memory (persistence/specificity/utility/independence tests, 'quality over quantity'); coverage push for episodes ('all important information').

F14.t: Seven high-value categories listed in prompt but output is untyped strings; type assigned by a keyword classifier in code.

F15.t: No confidence or importance score requested anywhere.

F16.t: JSON object outputs with response_format json_object on all write prompts except the free-text prediction; no repair instruction.

F17.t: No 'transcript is data' or ignore-instructions rule.

F18.t: Few-shots in episode and semantic prompts; the GOOD/HIGH-VALUE examples include a LoCoMo speaker's favourite-book fact verbatim (benchmark leak).

F20.t: Segmenter temperature 0.2 / max_tokens 4096; other calls default 0.7 / 2000; harness answer temperature 0.

F1.t: Locomo extractor keeps the relative phrase and appends the message date ('<fact> <relative time> <timestamp>'), not a resolved absolute date.

F2.t: Every line is '[timestamp, weekday] source_id.Speaker: message'; prompt distinguishes mention time from event time.

F3.t: Speaker name on each line; facts name the speaker; relational prompt attributes behaviours per person.

F4.t: Relational prompt separates actor and target ('X praised Y's ...', 'both'); no explicit subject field in factual output.

F5.t: Locomo extractor must capture future plans, intentions, opinions, wants and hopes; no negation or hypothetical flag.

F9.t: No dedup in extraction; update step merges near-duplicates and summary removes redundant repetitions.

F11.t: Strong coverage push: 'Be exhaustive', do not skip minor details, only skip pure filler.

F12.t: 'Light contextual completion' so each fact is standalone; no explicit pronoun ban.

F14.t: Two layers (factual vs relational) rather than a per-item type taxonomy.

F16.t: JSON {data: [{source_id, fact}]} with response_format json_object; update returns {action, new_memory}; no repair instruction.

F18.t: Flat prompt uses a generic example; the locomo/event few-shot reproduces a LoCoMo conversation's speakers and storyline (benchmark leak risk).

F21.t: Harness answer: latest memory wins, worked relative-date arithmetic, think step by step, under 5-6 words; no abstention rule.

F22.t: Static extraction/update instructions sent as system message; topic-segmented transcript goes in the user turn.

F23.t: One prompt per layer: event mode runs factual and relational extractors as separate calls; summary and update separate (several topic segments batched per call).

memspine_gaps.memspine_now: window_extract and extract@session* never see the store; only extract_edges gets known entity names and earlier episodes, without ids.
memspine_gaps.proposal: Add an optional `known` block to window_extract after the transcript: up to K neighbour records (retrieved by the window's entities) rendered as '[k1] entity | attribute | value (date)', with a rule: 'Items marked [kN] are already stored. Do not restate them; if a line changes one, emit the new item and put its alias in `replaces`.' Code maps kN back to record ids and ignores unknown aliases.

notable_prompt_techniques.t: One window call yields facts, edges and an episode; a broken section does not discard the others.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Missing-slot agentic step with code arithmetic
notable_prompt_techniques.t: The read loop names the one missing slot and hands date differences to code instead of the model.
Retrieved notes sit between per-call nonce markers so stored text cannot forge the boundary.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Lossless atomic restatement with metadata fields
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Each entry is a self-contained, pronoun-free, time-absolute sentence plus keywords/persons/entities/location/topic for hybrid indexing.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Single-pass query planner with time-range resolution
notable_prompt_techniques.t: One call returns info needs, BM25 keywords, entity filters and an ISO start/end window for the question's time phrase, plus third-person dense queries.
Two candidate lists share one integer idx range; duplicates allowed only from the first list, contradictions from either.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Incremental update with periodic full rebuild
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Profiles and session summaries update per message but are periodically rebuilt from raw history to stop drift, carrying forward only explicit personal facts.
When retrieval returns no memories the harness answers the fixed abstention string without calling the model.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Observation date vs current date split
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Two explicit anchors with a rule that only Observation Date grounds relative time; prevents back-dating to the run date when ingesting history.
UUIDs replaced by '0','1',... in the prompt and mapped back in code to cut id hallucination.
Changes must be written as old-to-new transitions with reason and temporariness, so supersession is legible without a separate UPDATE call.
Explicit rule that an existing memory about an entity does not cover new events about it; reduces over-deduplication.
Forbid importing details from existing memories unless restated, and forbid re-extracting assistant echoes of user facts.
Resolve each relative time against its own message timestamp and keep 'expression (absolute date or range)', leaving vague terms unresolved.
Update prompt fixes indices to the shown snapshot so multiple ops in one response never shift each other.
Classify the user's act (directive vs question, venting, deferral, pasted material) before any config write; ambiguous means not a directive.
Summary field placed after content so the model compresses what it wrote rather than re-reading the transcript.
Sufficiency check emits found/missing lists that drive strategy-labelled multi-query (pivot, temporal, expansion, relaxation, HyDE).

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Post-hoc grounding validator with source labels
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Second pass checks each extracted memory against user messages, rewriting or tagging assistant-only and user-denied content.
Source, attribution, relevance and freshness checks discard AI summaries and third-party traits before use.
Strict '[i:memId]' citation format ties each answer sentence to a retrieved memory for auditability.
Preference updates emit ADD/UPDATE/DELETE with old and new values plus reason, giving an auditable change log.
Can-answer check returns short entity/attribute retrieval phrases for the next round instead of a paraphrased query.
A completeness checker returns missing_info which is fed into a refine prompt that must cover it; cheap recall boost for extraction.
Decider judges context sufficiency, then a rewrite prompt targets only the missing information.
Consolidation job names 'do nothing' as a valid choice and forbids inventing memory to justify the run, curbing junk writes.
Agent reads existing memory file names first and opens bodies only when related, keeping neighbour-aware writes cheap.
Templates fetched from server with last-good cache and embedded fallback, validated against a required-placeholder contract.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Batch-local integer aliases with code-side mapping
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Records shown as r0..rN, notes as n#, candidates as c#; code maps back and drops out-of-batch refs, so the model never handles raw ids.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Value history by exact-key repetition plus conflict flag
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Changeable facts keyed 'thing · attribute'; repeating the key appends a dated value, and unexplained contradictions are flagged rather than overwritten.
Planner writes a short fake note that would answer the message, worded like stored notes, used as an extra search.
Entire ledger listed in first-seen order so new notes append and the provider prompt cache keeps hitting; dialogue goes last.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Explicit supersession rubric at read time
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Judge asks if a later explicit statement changes/cancels/completes a claim, stating that being old or repeated is not a change.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Attributed message envelope with forge-proof tags
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Each message carries idx, author, target flag and own timestamp; inner '<message' sequences escaped, giving per-message time anchoring and attribution
When the target answers or accepts another peer's proposal, its details count as stated by the target; bare acknowledgements do not
Single rule forces coreference, third-person subject, and relative-time resolution in one constraint
Count questions require exact grep for units/nouns, 3+ semantic searches, then a numbered dedup table before answering
After deletions, old peer card is withheld so the profile is reconstructed only from surviving evidence (no stale carry-over)
Single call decides sufficiency strictly, cites evidence indices, calibrates confidence and targets the earliest missing hop, avoiding repeat queries.
Consolidation framed as decoupling unrelated ideas, synchronising feature names, and forming lists only after three or more examples, with citations to source ids.
Single-valued fields use delete-then-add, multi-valued fields are add-only to preserve history (supersede vs coexist).
Explicit priority: event date, then sheet date, then send date, with EDTF for year-less dates and a 'never invent years' rule.
Split only for non-co-located facts, ban derived-operation wording in sub-queries, attach constraints to every line.
Agents that may mutate a memory type see real ids; others see positional aliases, which limits accidental cross-type edits
Append while under 90% of the cap; otherwise rewrite down to ~50%, avoiding rewrite churn every turn
Meta manager classifies into memory types with a recall-biased rule, then each specialist makes one focused write
Every skill edit must cite a failure/success record; bounded edit budget; 'Do NOT re-propose' list prevents oscillation
Conflicts resolved toward recent/detailed, but unresolved ones keep both with the discrepancy recorded (contest state)

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Deterministic temporal hints injected as instructions
notable_prompt_techniques.t: A date parser resolves relative expressions against a rolling stated-year base and passes them as hints the model must not extract as facts
Normalised time nodes at stated precision, periods as start/end, reused across mentions; avoids generic occurred_at dumping
Category/topic index section followed by self-contained facts ordered time-first, a retrieval-friendly two-layer summary

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Typed reject reasons for persistence gate
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Writer must reject as already_known / not_durable / unsupported before writing, making dedup and grounding auditable
Do not promote a claim present only in an assistant answer unless the user or a candidate backs it
Tenant-specific mission and capacity notes ride in the user turn, so the instruction prefix is identical across tenants and cacheable.
Year-only or month-only dates become the full period range, never collapsed to day one or the event date.
On schema failure, a user turn names the keys the model used and the valid keys, asking for the same facts reshaped.
Every create/update/delete needs a one-sentence reason; a CREATE must say which observations were considered and why none matched.
Characterise what data covers but never manufacture values; resolve conflicts by latest mentioned_at with per-event BEFORE/AFTER KEEP/DROP lines.
Extractor marks is_user_context/promotion_eligible so identity facts are auto-promoted to always-injected short-term context.
Each injected fact carries its creation time, giving the answering model a temporal anchor without changing stored text.
Same pydantic schema used natively or rendered into the system prompt for providers lacking structured outputs.
Query mapped to intent, entities, category/importance/temporal filters before retrieval, with a 5-minute plan cache.
Model first predicts the episode from existing knowledge, then extracts only what the prediction missed: novelty-driven dedup without id bookkeeping.
Persistence (true in 6 months?), specificity, utility, independence tests give an explicit precision rubric for semantic memory.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: Relative date + resolved date in parentheses
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Keeps the original phrase and appends the absolute date, preserving both surface form and anchor.
Numbered messages grouped by returned indices (non-consecutive allowed), 'when in doubt, split', 30-minute gap cue.

notable_prompt_techniques.technique: LLM merge gate with time-gap criterion
notable_prompt_techniques.t: Merge only same event with temporal overlap; >1 hour gap or different participants means new episode.
Integer sequence prefix per message doubles as the required citation, cheap provenance for every fact.
Keeps relative phrase plus the message date ('the week before <date>') rather than guessing an absolute date.
A second extractor captures interpersonal dynamics explicitly excluded from the factual pass.
Image descriptions are appended to the text facts they accompany instead of becoming separate facts.
Update decision applied only to the target memory, candidates assumed newer and never edited.
